In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
area-averaging of point pressures reduces the high frequency components and increases low frequency components in the external pressures.
the area-averaging process has the effect of smoothing out high-frequency components of pressure fluctuations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the peak values of point pressures are always greater than the peak values of area-averaged external pressures for all the wind directions.
the point pressure data can be used for the design of the building envelope and the area-averages can be used for structural analysis of the building.
the peak and RMS values for point pressures on the windwall of a low-rise building are always higher than those of the corresponding area-averaged values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the area-averaging of point pressures is not a reliable technique to obtain area-averaged external pressures on the wall of the building.
area-averaged pressure data are not a good representation of the true behaviour of the point pressures and should be used cautiously.
the area-averaging procedure is not a suitable method to reduce the peak and RMS values of point pressures.
